review_evidence: codex self-review: pedagogy, grammar, ambiguity, grading, passage independence, and age fit
title: It is Fun
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Move like an animal
levels.teaching_goal: Connect hop, crawl, glide, trot, and swing with the movements they name.

guided_check.teaching_block: Movement words are precise. Worked example: a rabbit hops with short jumps; it does not glide. Match the body movement, not only the animal.
guided_check.passage: A tiny frog makes short jumps from stone to stone.
guided_check.prompt: Which movement word matches the frog's short jumps?

bridge.teaching_block: “Glide” means moving smoothly. A bird may flap first, then glide with still wings.
bridge.passage: The kite moves smoothly across the open sky without jerking.
bridge.prompt: Which word best describes the movement?

masterclass.teaching_block: A trot uses quick, even steps. Do not choose “run” only because the animal is moving quickly.
masterclass.passage: The pony moves around the ring with quick, even steps.

independent_check.teaching_block: Name the movement from the body clue without choices.
independent_check.passage: A caterpillar moves slowly along a leaf with its body close to the surface.
independent_check.prompt: Name the movement shown by the caterpillar.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer movement vocabulary from animals to a playground object.
transfer_check.passage: A child holds the ropes and moves back and forth through the air.
transfer_check.prompt: Which movement word describes the child?

levels.title: Actions make the game lively
levels.teaching_goal: Find the word that tells what a child, animal, or object does.

guided_check.teaching_block: Ask “What happens?” Worked example: in “Cats stretch,” stretch is the action. An animal name answers who, not what happens.
guided_check.passage: The children leap over a chalk line.

bridge.teaching_block: A describing word can sit beside an action word. In “The quick bird flies,” quick describes and flies acts.
bridge.passage: A playful monkey climbs the low branch.
bridge.prompt: Which word tells what the monkey does?

masterclass.teaching_block: When two actions appear, use the person named in the question to select the right one.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the action test without choices.
independent_check.passage: The ducks paddle across the pond.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the verb skill from animal play to music time.
transfer_check.passage: The class taps the table to make a beat.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the word that shows the class action.

levels.title: Who can do what?
levels.focus: read an ability sentence and find the correct doer
levels.teaching_goal: Read can-sentences carefully and match each ability with the person or animal that has it.

guided_check.teaching_block: The word “can” tells an ability. Worked example: “A fish can swim” says the fish has the ability; it does not say every animal can swim.
guided_check.passage: A squirrel can climb the rough tree. A duck can cross the pond.
guided_check.prompt: Which animal can climb the tree?

bridge.teaching_block: Keep the two abilities separate. Find the exact action asked in the question.
bridge.passage: Nima can balance on one foot. Her brother can roll a hoop.
accepted_answers: she can balance on one foot

masterclass.teaching_block: A negative clue changes the meaning. “Cannot fly” does not remove the ability stated after “can.”
masterclass.passage: An ostrich cannot fly, but it can run quickly.

independent_check.teaching_block: Answer from the stated ability only.
independent_check.passage: Rehan can copy the slow walk of a tortoise.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer ability reading from movement play to making something.
transfer_check.passage: Lopa can fold a paper bird. Manu can paint its wings.

levels.title: Build an “I can” sentence
levels.focus: arrange words into a complete ability sentence
levels.teaching_goal: Place I first, can next, and the action after can to make a clear ability sentence.

guided_check.teaching_block: The pattern is I + can + action. Worked example: “draw / can / I” becomes “I can draw.” Do not add “am” after can.
guided_check.passage: Words: I / can / hop / like a frog
options: I can hop like a frog.
I hop can like a frog.
accepted_answers: I can hop like a frog.
i can hop like a frog

bridge.teaching_block: Keep the action phrase together. “Across the mat” belongs after crawl.
bridge.passage: Words: can / across the mat / I / crawl
options: I can crawl across the mat.
I across can crawl the mat.
Can the mat I across crawl.
accepted_answers: I can crawl across the mat.
i can crawl across the mat

masterclass.teaching_block: When another person is the subject, use that name first but keep can before the action.

independent_check.teaching_block: Build the ability sentence without choices.
independent_check.passage: Words: like a bird / I / can / stretch
independent_check.prompt: Arrange the words to tell what you can do like a bird.
accepted_answers: I can stretch like a bird.
i can stretch like a bird

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the pattern to a classroom skill instead of a movement.
transfer_check.passage: Words: a short poem / can / read / I
transfer_check.prompt: Arrange the words to tell a classroom reading skill.
accepted_answers: I can read a short poem.
i can read a short poem

levels.title: Make a playful comparison
levels.focus: write a complete sentence comparing an action with an animal
levels.teaching_goal: Write a sentence with a doer, an action, and a like-comparison that makes sense.

guided_check.teaching_block: A comparison joins a real action to a clear image. Worked example: “I stretch like a cat.” names who, what, and the comparison.
guided_check.passage: Ravi takes one large, heavy step during the action game.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence makes a sensible comparison?

bridge.teaching_block: The animal should match the movement. A butterfly can flutter; a stone cannot.
bridge.passage: Mina moves her arms lightly and quickly.

masterclass.teaching_block: A complete comparison still needs a sensible action. Check meaning as well as sentence shape.
masterclass.passage: The child moves slowly with hands and feet close to the floor.
options: The child crawls like a tortoise.
The child flies like a spoon.
accepted_answers: The child crawls like a tortoise.
the child crawls like a tortoise

independent_check.teaching_block: Create your own comparison. Include I, one movement, and an animal that can reasonably move that way.
independent_check.passage: During the game, you choose a movement that you can act out safely.
independent_check.prompt: Write one “I” sentence with an action and a like-comparison.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer comparison writing from animals to weather. Keep the sentence complete and the image sensible.
transfer_check.passage: A ribbon moves gently in the wind.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one sentence comparing the ribbon’s movement with something else that moves gently.

items.passage: Neha bends while Omar stretches.
The horse gallops across the field.
A penguin can waddle. A seal can clap its flippers.

items.prompt: Which animal shape can Vani make?

items.passage: Words: I / can / balance / carefully
Words: can / the duck / swim
Words: like a monkey / can / Rohit / climb
options: Rohit can climb like a monkey.
accepted_answers: Rohit can climb like a monkey.
rohit can climb like a monkey

items.passage: Words: can / we / together / march
Jatin moves with slow, heavy steps.
Leena makes quick little jumps.
A paper plane moves smoothly through the room.
options: The plane glides like a bird.
The plane digs like a mole.
accepted_answers: The plane glides like a bird.
the plane glides like a bird

items.passage: You choose a safe movement for the class action circle.
items.prompt: Write a complete sentence comparing your movement with an animal.
